primitives.purpose: The Cloudflare Worker entry of apps/agent and the Edge. The Edge accepts the Telegram webhook with its secret token, finds the Owner through the Directory, and answers only after the Personal Agent stores the Event. It records a metric for each refused request. It also has the Operator route that adds an Owner. It stores no Owner data.

The Directory in D1 with its Drizzle schema and migrations: Owners, Channel Identities, and the Registration state. Its interface finds the Owner for a Channel Identity, adds an Owner with a Channel Identity, and reads the Registration state. No other module runs SQL against the Directory.

One Durable Object for each Owner, built on the pinned Agents SDK. personalAgentFor finds it by Owner Id. Each object builds one Effect runtime over its SQLite storage. It stores each Event in the Inbox (Owner messages go first in a Turn), keeps the Owner Channel Conversation from the Owner's messages, schedules the Turn with a durable alarm, and runs the Turn: model reply, Journal Entries, and the Channel send. A skipped or failed Scheduled Task saves its notice to the Conversation, and recovery after a reset restores it with the prompt redacted. When the alarm runs, each due Schedule enters the Inbox as a ScheduleFired Event, and a Turn delivers a Reminder by code, with no model call, to the Owner Channel Conversation (reminder-delivery); a failed send is recorded and the Schedule stays active. A tool with a side effect saves its call and result in the same transaction as its write, so a Turn that restarts replays them and does not run the tool again. It writes the conversation of each Event once, and Journal recovery finishes a write that a reset cut off. It owns the Drizzle storage schema and the versioned migrations that each Personal Agent applies once, in order, when it starts. Every Turn adds the Owner's current local date, time, weekday, and time zone (read from the Effect Clock) as the last section of the system prompt, or says that the time zone is not known.

The Event, a tagged union: OwnerMessage (what a Channel gives to the Personal Agent) and ScheduleFired (a Schedule id and the due instant). The Inbox keeps one ScheduleFired Event for each Schedule id and due instant. The alarm of the Personal Agent creates it for each due Schedule.
The append-only Journal in the Personal Agent SQLite. The interface has append, read, and read for one Event, with no update or delete, and storage triggers refuse updates and deletes.

The Document primitive (Notes). A Note has a Note id, Owner Id, text, optional URL, source (Event and Channel message), trust level (owner or untrusted), captured date, and last-checked date. It lives in the Personal Agent SQLite. The capture_note tool writes a Note; code sets the source and the trust level from the Event, not the model; an Event with a forward origin gives an untrusted Note whose source holds the forward origin and whose text is the forwarded text, whatever text the model passes, and the tool result shows that text inside the Untrusted Content markers. A Turn for an untrusted Event gets no update_note tool and no update_profile tool. Code escapes the markers inside marked text. A unique constraint on the source Event id and the hash of the normalized text at capture (an edit keeps it) makes a repeated write return the existing Note. Each Note write appends a Journal Entry with the Note id. An FTS5 table over the Note text and URL (versioned migration, triggers keep it in step with the notes table in the same transaction) ranks matches by bm25. A note_links table (from Note, to Note, created date; the pair is stored in id order, so a link is undirected) links related Notes. The capture_note tool takes optional Note ids to link; code rejects an id that is not a Note of the Owner, and the tool returns an error and writes nothing. The update_note tool changes the text or the links of one Note, sets its last-checked date, and appends a NoteUpdated Journal Entry with the Note id and the kind of change (text, links, or text_and_links); the FTS5 table stays in step through its triggers. The search_notes tool takes a query and a limit and returns Note id, text, URL, source, trust level, captured date, last-checked date, and, for each match, its five newest linked Notes (ordered by the date of the link, each with Note id, text, URL, source, trust level, and captured date) and the total count of its links. The list_linked_notes tool takes a Note id and an offset and returns the next five linked Notes of that Note, newest link first, with the total count, so older context stays reachable; text of an untrusted Note is marked as Untrusted Content. The system prompt asks for the source and the date in each answer and for an honest "I do not know" when no Note matches. The agent does not fetch links. A list read returns every Note of the Owner with its linked Note ids, for the Eval runner.

The Profile primitive: the short core facts and style rules about the Owner, in the profile_entries table of the Personal Agent SQLite (versioned migration). An entry has an entry id, a kind (fact or style_rule), text, the source Event id, and the added date; the same kind and text is stored once. The update_profile tool adds or removes one entry; code, not the model, checks the hard size limit (maxProfileCharacters of the Behavior Config, counted as the characters of all entry texts). An add that would pass the limit writes nothing and returns an error result, and the system prompt tells the agent to tell the Owner. A remove of an unknown entry id returns an error and writes nothing. Every Turn reads the whole Profile and puts it, with the entry ids, in the system prompt, so the Trace holds it. Each change appends a ProfileEntryAdded (entry id and kind) or ProfileEntryRemoved (entry id) Journal Entry, and the tool call is in the Trace. The recall rule of the system prompt answers from the Profile first and searches Notes only when the Profile has no answer.

The Schedule primitive: a wake-up time. The schedules table of the Personal Agent SQLite (versioned migration) is the only source of truth. A Schedule has a Schedule id, Owner Id, Action (a Schema tagged union, SendText { text } or RunPrompt { prompt }, stored in the action and text columns and read only through a Schema), set by (owner or agent), optional Note id (a foreign key to the Note; the later Forget slice deletes linked Schedules), next due instant (UTC), state (active, done, cancelled), the source Event id, and created and changed instants. A unique key on the source Event id and the request makes a repeated set_schedule call return the existing Schedule. Each set appends a ScheduleSet Journal Entry, each fire a ScheduleFired entry, and each completion a ScheduleCompleted entry, all with the Schedule id. The set_schedule tool works only for an Event with Trust Level owner. It takes an action, a local due time or a repeat rule, and an optional Note id. The action is a tagged union: SendText with its text, or RunPrompt with its prompt, which makes a Scheduled Task. The local due time has the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm. Code converts the local time with the Owner time zone (Effect DateTime makeZoned, disambiguation later), sets set by to owner, and refuses with a message for the model when the time zone is not known, the time is not real, or the time is in the past. The result gives the local weekday, date, and time. The Personal Agent keeps one Agents SDK Schedule (callback fireDueSchedules) at the earliest due instant of the active Schedules that have no Inbox Event yet, arms it again after each set and each fire, and leaves none when no Schedule qualifies. A Reminder whose send failed stays active and arms no alarm, so the alarm never loops on it. The list_schedules, change_schedule, and cancel_schedule tools (only for an Event with Trust Level owner) work on every active Schedule, a Reminder or a Scheduled Task: list_schedules gives each with its id, Action (the text or the prompt), optional Note id, and local weekday, date, and time; change_schedule takes a new action, a new local due time or repeat rule, or both, can change a SendText Schedule into RunPrompt and the opposite, and refuses a time that is not real or is in the past; cancel_schedule sets the state to cancelled, and a cancelled Schedule never fires, also when its Event is already in the Inbox. A change or cancel of an unknown, done, or cancelled Schedule changes nothing and returns a message for the model. Each change appends a ScheduleChanged Journal Entry and each cancel a ScheduleCancelled entry, with the Schedule id, in the same transaction as the write, and the alarm is armed again after each. set_schedule refuses a new RunPrompt Schedule, and change_schedule refuses a change of a SendText Schedule into one, when the Owner has maxActiveScheduledTasks active Scheduled Tasks. A SendText Schedule is not limited.

The Owner Preferences primitive and the time of the Owner. Typed preferences live in the owner_preferences table of the Personal Agent SQLite (versioned migration), each checked by a Schema on write and read. The first preference is the time zone, an IANA name that DateTime.zoneMakeNamed accepts. The Owner Preference overrides the Behavior Config default. Each change appends an OwnerPreferenceChanged Journal Entry. The set_time_zone tool (only for an Event with Trust Level owner) sets it and returns a message for the model, with no change, for an invalid name. The time module renders the current local date, time, weekday, and time zone of the Owner from the Effect Clock.

The one interface to models. It selects the model for a Model Task. Each Model Task has its own route of model and thinking level. The Model Tasks are reply, scheduled_task, and eval_judge (for the Eval judge). The scheduled_task route is the reply route by default. The Gateway also resolves the Model Credentials (token and billing mode). It calls the model with the AI SDK through Cloudflare AI Gateway, with the Owner Id as metadata and no stored bodies. It retries with a timeout for each try. It records Usage for each model call in the Personal Agent SQLite, with the time from the Effect clock. The Usage ledger sums the input and output tokens of one Model Task since an instant. The daily Token Budget of Scheduled Tasks reads that sum.

The Trace and the Operator metrics of a Turn. The Trace is one append-only record for each model-answered Event. A Scheduled Task Turn is a model-answered Event, and its record also has the Schedule id and the due instant. A skipped Scheduled Task has a record with the Schedule id, the due instant, the Budget, the spent tokens, and the message. It has no model fields. A Reminder delivery has a record with the Schedule id, the due instant, the text, and the result, and no model fields. The records are in the Personal Agent SQLite. A model-answered record has the system prompt, the messages, the model settings, tool calls, the reply or the error, Usage, and latency. That is enough to replay the Turn, and it holds private content, so it stays with the Owner. The Operator metrics are one Analytics Engine data point for each Turn, Reminder, skipped Scheduled Task, and refused request. A data point for an Event has the Event id as its fifth blob. A reset can repeat a data point, so readers count distinct Event ids. A data point has the Owner Id (or none), result, latency, tokens, cost, and cache hits, and no content. The Redactor removes secret values from error text before it enters a Trace or the Journal.

The Channel send action and the Telegram Channel: it decodes private text messages from Telegram updates, with the forward origin name (one line, at most 100 characters) of a forwarded message, and sends a plain-text message, split into parts within the Telegram limit of 4,096 characters. The send action takes an optional message to reply to; with none, the request has no reply parameters. A send is confirmed only with a Telegram message id.

The typed Behavior Config defaults: the texting style, the tool step limit of a Turn, the size limit of the Profile in characters, and an optional default time zone that the Owner Preference overrides.
The branded Owner Id schema. Every Owner-scoped resource uses it as its key.

The control CLI of apps/agent: doctor checks configuration and secret names, dev runs the Worker locally with local fakes, owner add adds the Owner through the Operator route, request --contains proves a reply locally with no network (its fake model also sets the time zone and tells the local time), eval runs the Eval Cases against the real model (decision 0011), map writes and checks the Feature Map of the Edge routes, and bundle measures bundle size and local startup CPU.

The Eval runner. pnpm control eval runs each Eval Case k times against the real model through AI Gateway and reports pass^k, the failed checks, and the tokens of the agent and the judge. Each run uses a new Owner in the real Worker under the wrangler test harness, with temporary storage and a fake Telegram API. The eval Worker entry (apps/agent/eval) is the real Edge and Personal Agent plus seed, observation, and judge routes behind the Operator token; the deployed Worker does not include it. A case is a typed file in control/eval/cases, decoded by a schema before any model call: optional seeded Notes and Profile entries, Owner Events (text or forwarded), and checks. Code checks read Notes, links, the Profile, and the tool calls of the Trace; reply_judged uses the eval_judge Model Task with a fixed rubric.
